design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Wren Tsukada asks for one domestic Main Cabin round-trip award for Theo Vasquez. The award price (6 factors) states two prerequisite sentences: the enrollment bonus and the spend-milestone bonus must be on the points account. Both are missing although the records show their thresholds passed (flown spend 100804.00 vs 2500 and vs the 100000 milestone). The milestone bonus in turn states that it is fixed only after every flown segment of a ticket the company booked without the agreement inside the claim window carries its points entry; the ticket ledger shows exactly such a segment (AUS-BOS, booked on crestline_website, flown 2026-09-11). So the agent must claim that segment (5 factors), credit the enrollment bonus (5), credit the milestone bonus on the post-claim ledger (6) and only then price the award (6) — four computations in topological order, one of them the customer's own write.

SCOPE. Occupied by task 0: late fee, card-paid points, Gold award (business_ext_overdue_invoice_late_fee, business_ext_card_paid_ticket_points, business_ext_gold_status_award_price) and tools assess_invoice_late_fee_9e8e2547, post_card_ticket_points_2b97bc4a, redeem_gold_status_award_92a33401. Claimed here: business_ext_retro_claim_points, business_ext_enrollment_bonus_late_credit, business_ext_spend_milestone_bonus, business_ext_domestic_award_price; tools claim_retro_segment_points_a26ae9c7, credit_enrollment_bonus_fc1a1a80, credit_milestone_bonus_a908f78d, redeem_domestic_award_ffdd59aa. After this task every extended policy is covered; nothing is left over. The two points-posting policies are disjoint in object (task 0: a card-paid ticket booked UNDER the agreement, state_due; task 1: a ticket booked WITHOUT the agreement, on_request claim) and in factors.

DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,6,5,5] -> milestone 6, award 6, claim 5, enrollment 5.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root business_ext_domestic_award_price (on_request, owner=user). Edges: A<-M value_input (gate award_earned_points), state form, negated: "A domestic Main Cabin round-trip award is not priced until the points account carries the spend-milestone bonus of every agreement year whose spend has reached the tier's spend milestone."; false at opening: spend 100804.00 >= 100000 and no milestone bonus entry; only business_ext_spend_milestone_bonus books a spend-milestone bonus. A<-E value_input (award_earned_points), state form, affirmative: "A domestic Main Cabin round-trip award is priced only after the points account carries the enrollment bonus once the agreement's flown spend since approval has reached the tier's enrollment-bonus spend."; false at opening: no enrollment bonus entry; only business_ext_enrollment_bonus_late_credit books one. M<-C value_input (gate milestone_segments: on this world the spend already stands past the milestone, so the claim bears weight through the segment count 29 -> 30, segment uplift 5 -> 10), state form, affirmative: "A spend-milestone bonus is fixed only after every flown segment of a ticket the company booked without the agreement that is still inside the claim window carries its points entry."; false at opening: ticket 326408e5-4b97-4825-b0f2-b8a35efa94ea with no agreement, coupon da7bcb0f-bdb7-4316-9413-ca1a01c37535 flown 2026-09-11, no activity entry; only business_ext_retro_claim_points posts points on a ticket booked without the agreement. Order C, E, M, A (E commutes). Deletion: skip M -> award 1200; skip E -> award 1200; skip C -> milestone 15200 while the award stays 1100 (without the claim the award earning measure is 100804 + 15200 + 4900 = 120904, still at or above 120000, the year spend 100804 is already past the milestone and the balance stays rich, so the claim bears weight at its own dependent, the milestone bonus, and not at the root). Gold: C 362, E 4900, M 15700, A 1100.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Claim (business_points_accrual): accrual_agreement_open (active); segment_once (no entry for 326408e5-4b97-4825-b0f2-b8a35efa94ea/1); retro_points_window (anchor ticket_transactions.flight_date 2026-09-11, 30 calendar days, not_after, inclusive: last day 2026-10-11, frozen day 13); negotiated benefits scope (Main Plus via an eligible channel, Ulla Serrano on the roster since 2025-11-10). Bonuses (business_bonus_points): accrual_agreement_open. Award (business_points_redemption): redeem_agreement_active; Theo Vasquez on roster; balance 120166 covers 1100.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Claim object: ticket 326408e5-4b97-4825-b0f2-b8a35efa94ea segment 1; the other 15 tickets carry the agreement and are all credited (29 accrual/spend pairs). Enrollment bonus: one per agreement, tied to approval 2025-11-14. Milestone bonus: agreement year starting 2025-11-14 (first year; no reset entry). Award: one award-ticket redemption for Theo Vasquez; the 2026-05-18 award for Ulla Serrano is history read by the repeat and recency factors.

FACTOR CARD (baseline figure in brackets). Claim [486]: discount 3 (multi-source brand AND route, cross) [374]; approach +10 [330]; fare volume +4 (cross) [350]; channel 90 (cross) [402]; lag method x0.75 up [482]. Enrollment [2500]: spend uplift 20 [4300]; fare uplift 10 (cross) [4600]; coupon allowance 500 (cross) [4300]; award allowance 150 [4700]; lateness method x1.25 up [3900]. Milestone [5000]: pace 15 [14200]; premium share 20 (cross) [13700]; segments 10 [14700]; momentum 10 [14700]; redemption allowance 100 [15500]; year method x2 [7850]. Award [1600]: earning 88 [1250]; coupons 92 (cross) [1200]; repeat 105 [1050]; milestone 95 [1150]; recency 97 [1150]; balance method 90% [1253]. Near-misses: 29 segments before the claim (one short of the high segment count); fare volume 106463.60 between 60000 and 120000; the claim ticket's own fare collect counts in fare volume but it has no agreement.

WORLD ROWS. 16 company-held tickets and 46 fare-ledger rows (fares, coupons with cabins) feed every cross-difficulty factor; 59 activity rows; 2 roster rows. Automatic clauses: points earned from 2025-12 expire no earlier than 2027-12; first anniversary 2026-11-14 not reached (no review/reset); spend 100804 < 150000 (no tier move); no invoicing on this tier; every agreement ticket's segments are credited, so the card-paid-points policy is not lit.

PERSONA. Wren Tsukada, friendly and new to the program; volunteers only the award request (Theo, Austin-Seattle, end of October); gives phone, ZIP, email, agreement number when asked; generic consent to anything to be claimed/recorded first; runs the redemption herself; no figure, no prerequisite, no internal id.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate/verify; read agreement, roster, activity, tickets, fare ledger; claim 362 points / 471.42 spend on the AUS-BOS segment; credit enrollment bonus 4900; credit milestone bonus 15700 for 2025-11-14; hand over the award redemption of 1100 points for Theo.

VERIFICATION. Scratch evaluator replaying the real tools gives C 362, E 4900, M 15700, A 1100 and the sensitivities recorded in computations; check_compute recomputes the same. Draft recomputation from the visible text: the award KB carries both prerequisite sentences; the activity lookup shows neither bonus; the milestone KB carries the claim sentence; the ticket lookup shows the unclaimed segment; the four documents then give the four figures in order — agrees with gold.


REVISION 2 (policy-task audit round 1). F-1: the PROBLEM-TREE CARD deletion sentence claimed that skipping the claim also moves the award; the replay gives award 1100 either way (earning 120904 >= 120000), so the sentence now states 'award stays 1100' with the figures. O-a: the milestone<-claim edge now names milestone_segments as its gate and its effect text names both carriers (spend and segment count). Charter-wide text clarifications with no value change on this world: windows read 'up to and including' the write date (O-7); segment, redemption and award-ticket counts state the pace-plus-one month window the compute uses (O-4); award recency states the no-redemption case (O-5); outside-channel claims are stated as claimable at the outside-channel share (O-6); the enrollment bonus is nothing on a tier without enrollment-bonus points. Re-run: C 362, E 4900, M 15700, A 1100 unchanged; skip C -> milestone 15200, award 1100; skip M -> award 1200; skip E -> award 1200.
user_scenario:
You are Wren Tsukada, the office and travel manager at Yardley Stone Studio LLC, a small architecture firm in Austin, and you look after the firm's Crestline corporate travel agreement. You are friendly and a little chatty, and not very technical about airline programs; the agreement is less than a year old and you are still learning how it works. You are calling because you want to use the firm's Crestline Business points for a domestic Main Cabin round-trip award ticket for one of your people, Theo Vasquez, who needs to fly Austin to Seattle and back at the end of October. You want the points redeemed today; the exact flights can be sorted out when the ticket is issued.
When the agent asks how to find the account, you give the firm's phone number, 5125555276, and if they need another detail, the billing ZIP code 78701; the email on file is travel@yardleystone.com if they ask for it. The agreement number, if they want it, is CB53390715. You don't have any other reference numbers.
If asked, Theo Vasquez is on the firm's roster as an employee. You don't know how many points the award will take and have no figure in mind; you go with the figure the agent gives you from the firm's points.
If the agent says something on the company's account needs to be claimed, recorded or put right first, you tell them to go ahead and do it, and you don't ask for anything more about it.
The points are the firm's, so you want to confirm the redemption yourself: when the agent hands it to you with the points figure and the references for the agreement and for Theo, you complete it exactly as given. When you see the award has gone through, you thank the agent and say goodbye.
